newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF mission arrives in Kiev for new credit talks.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission arrives in Kiev for new credit talks.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission arrived in Kiev on Tuesday to discuss a long-term credit programme and Ukraine's request for a stabilisation fund to underpin its new hryvnia currency, Fund officials said.

The talks would concentrate on granting a $2.5-3 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) for three years, to succeed the $867 million stand-by programme which is being disbursed in monthly tranches and set to extend into early 1997.
IMF officials have said previously the EFF might not be in place until the end of the year.
The IMF congratulated Ukraine on introduction of the hryvnia this month, but made no comment on Ukraine's request for the $1.5 billion stabilisation fund.

Ukrainian officials appeared confident of receiving the stabilisation fund for the hryvnia, introduced on September 2. The interim karbovanets currency was officially taken out of circulation on Tuesday.
Fund missions have been visiting Ukraine each month to review economic progress and approve monthly disbursements under the stand-by programme.

Ukraine has borrowed about $485 million under the terms of the stand-by loan, approved in May, and secured about $2 billion in IMF credits since winning approval for its first post-Soviet market reform programme in 1994. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
